q: Name the clause in the SQL standard that specifies the search order for a recursive CTE (breadth-first or depth-first).
What is the output of this code?
c:
WITH RECURSIVE power_set AS (
  SELECT ARRAY[1] AS subset
  UNION ALL
  SELECT p.subset || ARRAY[e.id]
  FROM power_set p
  CROSS JOIN (SELECT id FROM elements WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT UNNEST(p.subset))) e
  WHERE array_length(p.subset, 1) < 2
)
SELECT subset FROM power_set;
o: Subsets of elements up to a certain size

q: When a query optimizer applies the 'elimination of redundant semi-joins' rule, it removes a semi-join if the _____ constraint guarantees existence.
What is the output of this code?
c:
WITH RECURSIVE descendants AS (
  SELECT id, name, parent_id, 1 AS depth, ARRAY[id] AS path
  FROM nodes
  WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM nodes sub WHERE sub.parent_id = nodes.id)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT n.id, n.name, n.parent_id, d.depth + 1, d.path || n.id
  FROM nodes n
  INNER JOIN descendants d ON n.id = d.parent_id
  WHERE NOT n.id = ANY(d.path)
)
SELECT name FROM descendants ORDER BY depth DESC LIMIT 1;
o: The deepest leaf node reachable from any root without cycles
The root node of the tree
The node with the most children

Name the relational algebra operator that a semi-join corresponds to in query execution plans.
What is the output of this code?
c:
WITH RECURSIVE graph_path AS (
  SELECT src, dst, 1 AS dist, ARRAY[src, dst] AS visited
  FROM edges
  UNION ALL
  SELECT g.src, e.dst, g.dist + 1, g.visited || e.dst
  FROM graph_path g
  INNER JOIN edges e ON g.dst = e.src
  WHERE NOT e.dst = ANY(g.visited) AND g.dist < 6
)
SELECT src, dst, MIN(dist) AS shortest
FROM graph_path
GROUP BY src, dst;
o: Shortest path up to 6 hops between node pairs
All possible paths regardless of length

q: The PostgreSQL query planner can automatically switch a CTE from materialized to inlined based on the number of references and estimated cost.
What is the output of this code?
c:
WITH RECURSIVE subsets AS (
  SELECT ARRAY[val] AS s, val AS max_val
  FROM (SELECT UNNEST(ARRAY[1,2,3]) AS val) t
  UNION ALL
  SELECT s.s || t.val, t.val
  FROM subsets s
  CROSS JOIN (SELECT UNNEST(ARRAY[1,2,3]) AS val) t
  WHERE t.val > s.max_val AND array_length(s.s, 1) < 3
)
SELECT s FROM subsets;
o: The power set including the empty set

q: Name the SQL/MED (Management of External Data) feature that allows a LATERAL subquery to push predicates to external data sources.
What is the output of this code?
c:
WITH RECURSIVE partition AS (
  SELECT id, name, parent_id,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY id) AS rn,
    1 AS level
  FROM categories WHERE parent_id IS NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT c.id, c.name, c.parent_id,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY c.id),
    p.level + 1
  FROM categories c
  INNER JOIN partition p ON c.parent_id = p.id
)
SELECT name, level FROM partition;
o: Category hierarchy with levels and row numbering per iteration set

q: In a recursive CTE, using LIMIT inside the recursive member is generally prohibited because it introduces _____ semantics incompatible with fixpoint iteration.
Name the type of execution plan node that implements a LEFT JOIN where unmatched rows from the right table produce NULLs.
The query optimizer may choose a 'merge semi-join' when both the outer and inner tables are already sorted on the join key.
What is the output of this code?
c:
WITH RECURSIVE floyd AS (
  SELECT src, dst, ARRAY[src, dst] AS path, 1 AS len
  FROM edges
  UNION ALL
  SELECT f.src, e.dst, f.path || e.dst, f.len + 1
  FROM floyd f
  INNER JOIN edges e ON f.dst = e.src
  WHERE NOT e.dst = ANY(f.path) AND f.len < 4
)
SELECT src, dst, MIN(len) AS min_hops
FROM floyd
GROUP BY src, dst
HAVING MIN(len) > 1;
o: All node pairs with indirect connections within 4 hops
The longest path between any two nodes
